fluff.overview: The Weapon Carrier is a sixty-ton tracked combat vehicle designed by SLDF engineers during the Star League Civil War as a rapidly produced fire support platform. Based on earlier Age of War primitive weapons carriers, the design was manufactured by Drago, Ltd. of Skye as one of many companies mass-producing vehicles to replace losses during the Amaris Coup. Unlike the Quikscell carrier family built around internal combustion engines and minimal protection, the Weapon Carrier utilized a fusion powerplant and ferro-fibrous armor, providing substantially greater survivability at the cost of higher production complexity.
fluff.capabilities:
The AC/20 variant replaces the LB-X autocannons with two Class 20 autocannons, transforming the Weapon Carrier into a devastating close-range ambush platform. A single LRM-5 launcher provides minimal long-range capability. Three tons of AC/20 ammunition limit sustained fire but the massive damage potential of twin Class 20 weapons can cripple most targets in a single salvo.

The same GM 180 fusion engine, Aldis Heavy Ferro-Fibrous armor, Initrode Widecom communications, and RCA Instatrac Mark VI targeting equip this variant. The heavy forward armor concentration suits the ambush role, though the thin rear armor makes retreat from failed ambush positions extremely dangerous.
fluff.deployment: The AC/20 variant earned a reputation as a feared ambush tank during the Star League Civil War, capable of destroying lighter targets outright with its twin Class 20 weapons. Surviving examples were highly prized during the Succession Wars for their devastating close-range firepower.
fluff.history:
The Weapon Carrier emerged during the Star League Civil War in 2775, when SLDF engineers needed rapidly deployable fire support vehicles to replace catastrophic losses suffered during the fighting against Amaris forces. Drago, Ltd. on Skye produced all three variants from a common chassis, each mounting different autocannon configurations to fill specific tactical roles. The LB-10X variant served as the baseline design, with the AC/20 version fulfilling an ambush role and the Ultra/5 providing sustained fire support.

The design's reliance on Star League-era technology proved its undoing. As the Succession Wars destroyed the industrial base needed to produce ferro-fibrous armor and advanced autocannon systems, production ceased during the early First Succession War. The Weapon Carrier was replaced in service by the cruder but more easily manufactured Quikscell carrier family, and surviving examples became increasingly rare battlefield finds. Design quirks including difficult maintenance requirements and poor workmanship from wartime rush production contributed to the type's rapid disappearance.
